result.title: Probabilistic Ship Trajectory Forecasting using Transformer Models on AIS Data
result.comment: Manuscript written in 2021. 16 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables
result.summary: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps. The heat maps are generated using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and encoded with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) before entering the Transformer models. The models are trained with quantile loss to efficiently obtain a model-aware prediction interval, as this is crucial for timely collision avoidance. The proposed model architectures are shown to greatly outperform previous work while the inclusion of local heat maps enables the prediction of vessel movement that is not otherwise indicated from the previous positions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究受限水域内水面船舶的轨迹预测：用 AIS 位置数据训练 Transformer 与 Performer，将由核密度估计生成的局部位置热力图经 CNN 编码后一并输入模型，并以分位数损失训练以获得预测区间，报告性能优于先前工作。
AI.relevance_reason: CNN 编码的空间热力图作为额外通道注入 Transformer，可供核查 LVR 中空间证据如何进入推理状态、是否真被答案使用（对应视觉旁路与信息坍缩问题）；分位数损失给出的预测区间也可对照 STOP 决策与不确定性建模。属远领域方法线索，迁移可行性需读原文核实。
